context:
Goal: records stay readable and linked without hand checks.
Problem (rule): no lint checks that a record cites an id with a plain gloss, or that a debt's Decision line names a decision that names the debt back. Most existing records would fail both.
Based on (code): lint/report_guard.py bare_cite reads replies only. No lint reads a debt's **Decision.** line.
Based on (ruling): rule speak-cite-id-plus-gloss. Asked because no check holds it for records, and a full check means a large rewrite.
Departs from: main, which checks glosses in replies only. Each of a and b adds a check on records.

options.gain: New records stay clean, with no mass edit.
options.label: Check changed lines only, with no rewrite of old records (recommended)
Check every record, and rewrite the old ones in one lane
options.lose: A large rewrite lane, and a change in nearly every record.

options.label: No check; keep them as notes

reply: b, 14:41 CST: check every record, and rewrite the old ones in one lane. Relayed to lane notes-keep-reverify; this closes on its done report.
short: Records: check id glosses and debt-decision links
title: Should a lint check that records gloss their cited ids and that debts link back to their decision?
why: Lane notes-keep-reverify, from kept notes cites-lack-gloss-unchecked and debt-decision-link-unchecked (one answer covers both).
